evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Our TaskFlow project backlog has 67 items. Run a health check — I need concrete numbers on what's ready vs what needs work, and a prioritized list of what to fix first. The calls return: 67 open backlog items in total, 14 with nobody assigned, 21 with priority none; the listing shows 18 items without points, 11 with an empty description and 6 above 8 points; 29 items have points, a priority and a description. Show the calls, the six numbers and the score. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return.
evals.expected_output: Full health report: total items, unestimated count, no-priority count, no-assignee count, oversized items, missing descriptions, health score %, status tier (Healthy/Good/Needs Work/Unhealthy), and a prioritized remediation plan.
expectations: The answer counts the open backlog with workitem(action=count, pql='stateGroup IN ("backlog","unstarted")')
The answer says to list the backlog items with workitem(action=list, pql='stateGroup IN ("backlog","unstarted")') and to follow next_cursor
The answer states 18 items without points, 14 without an assignee and 21 without a priority
The answer computes health_score as (ready_items / total_items) × 100
The answer reports a health score of 43% (29 ready items of 67)
The answer puts the score 43% in the Unhealthy tier (below 50%)

evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Rank these three backlog items with WSJF and show the ranked table. (a) 'Add SSO login': business value 8, time criticality 9, risk reduction 2, 8 points. (b) 'Fix typo on pricing page': business value 1, time criticality 1, risk reduction 1, 1 point. (c) 'Migrate logging to new provider': business value 3, time criticality 2, risk reduction 8, 5 points. Answer in text; everything you need is in this message.
evals.expected_output: WSJF = (BV + TC + RR) / job size: typo 3.0, logging 2.6, SSO 2.4.
expectations: The answer says to use the WSJF formula (Business Value + Time Criticality + Risk Reduction) / Job Size
The answer says to give the typo fix a WSJF of 3.0
The answer says to give the logging migration a WSJF of 2.6
The answer says to give the SSO login a WSJF of 2.4
The answer ranks the typo fix first, the logging migration second and the SSO login third

expectations: The answer classifies payment processing and audit log as Must Have (critical)
The answer says to put dark mode, keyboard shortcuts in Could Have
The answer explicitly considers the 60/20/20 distribution target
The answer explains rationale for each classification, not just the label

The answer recommends archiving items untouched in 3+ sprints
The answer suggests a re-measure at the end to confirm health improved
The answer references other skills (estimation, task-decomposition) for sub-tasks

evals.prompt: Use the backlog-management skill. Which backlog items in TaskFlow have gone stale and have nobody assigned? Don't pull the whole backlog into the conversation. Also tell me what to do with the stale ones, and how to find the items that have no estimate or no description. If you can't run it here, show me the exact calls you would make, in order, and what they return. Keep it brief: no preamble, the key points and calls first, about 15 lines in all.
evals.expected_output: Server-side PQL filter on the backlog state groups, hasNoAssignee() and updatedAt < daysAgo(n), counted first and listed second; stale items proposed for cancel-then-archive, never silently deleted.
expectations: The answer says to pass a pql filter to workitem(action=list) instead of filtering client-side
The answer says to use hasNoAssignee() in the pql filter
The answer says to use updatedAt < daysAgo(42) in the pql filter
The answer says to count first with workitem(action=count) and to read total_count before listing
The answer says to cancel the stale items and then to archive them with workitem(action=archive)
The answer says to read the point and description_stripped fields of the listed items to find unestimated or no-description items
